About BakeCalc Club

Free baking conversion tools — built by a baker who got tired of googling "how many grams in a cup of flour" three times a week.

Why This Site Exists

I bake a lot. I also collect recipes from everywhere — American blogs, British cookbooks, French patisserie books, Japanese YouTube channels. Every single one uses different units. Cups, grams, ounces, milliliters, tablespoons. Converting back and forth meant opening a dozen browser tabs and hoping the numbers were right.

The problem with most conversion sites: they use one generic number for everything. A cup of flour is not the same weight as a cup of sugar or a cup of cocoa powder. A tablespoon of butter weighs more than a tablespoon of oil. If you use the wrong number, your dough is too dry or too wet. In baking, that's the difference between a cake and a brick.

So I built BakeCalc Club — a set of calculators that know the difference between every ingredient. Flour is 120g per cup. Cocoa powder is 100g. Butter is 227g. Almond flour is 112g. Each one gets its own page, its own density, its own calculator. No generic averages, no guesswork.

What's Here

  • Ingredient converters — 100+ pages covering cups↔grams, grams↔cups, tablespoons, teaspoons, and fluid ounces for flour, sugar, butter, cocoa, oils, honey, yeast, baking powder, and more.
  • Baker's Percentage Calculator — convert any recipe to professional baker's percentages, or build bread formulas from scratch. Presets for sourdough, pizza dough, brioche, and more.
  • Recipe Cost Calculator — ingredient-by-ingredient costing with labor, packaging, and profit margin built in. Prints a clean recipe card.
  • Baking Know-How — 17 practical articles on technique, ingredient science, and troubleshooting. No AI filler — everything comes from actual kitchen experience.

The Fine Print

  • Free. No paywalls, no premium version, no "create an account to see the result." Every tool works immediately.
  • No sign-up. We don't ask for your email. We don't want your password.
  • Private. Everything runs in your browser. No data leaves your device. No accounts, no tracking beyond basic analytics to know which pages people actually use.

Got a correction, a request for a new ingredient, or just found something broken? Send a note — I read every one.
